name: Creation Mart
summary: A working creator marketplace that connects precise production briefs to creators through production passports, explainable matching, rights fit receipts, and reviewed private delivery. Brands can evaluate how work is made, why a creator fits, and which declared uses are supported before selecting a creator.

usps.title: U1 · Production Passports
usps.description: Published portfolio items combine real media previews with declared skills, tools, model pipeline, workflow, capabilities, usage offers and supporting claim evidence. The reserve → upload → finalize → publish pipeline checks actual bytes, hashes, media headers and image dimensions. Evidence can become stale when the underlying work changes. Public portfolio visibility and private evidence access are controlled separately.

usps.title: U2 · Explainable Brief Fit
usps.description: SQL-backed creator discovery supports text, specialties, skills, tools, models, media kinds, formats, aspect ratios, styles, languages, availability, budget, currency and rights state. Brief-aware eligibility checks capability combinations, not unrelated individual tags. Fit-v1 exposes outcomes (35), style (20), workflow (15), format (15), availability (5), and evidence (10) terms. Applicable weights are normalized into a score with component numerators, denominators and reasons. Brands persist private shortlists and compare up to three creators.

usps.title: U3 · Rights Fit Receipts
usps.description: A reproducible receipt compares the brief's requested commercial use, paid ads, modifications, source files, exclusivity, training use, attribution, territories and duration with creator declarations, model references and final delivery permissions. Each rule identifies its source and explanation. Outcomes are compatible_declared, needs_review or blocked. SQL and TypeScript implementations are covered by parity fixtures; final acceptance checks actual submission scope and permissions.

usps.title: U4 · Executable Brief Copilot
usps.description: A persistent six-section brief builder now calls a real language model through Vercel AI Gateway to generate suggested production drafts, refine creative direction and analyze conflicts and missing answers. Structured outputs are schema-checked and catalog-validated, then evaluated by deterministic publication rules. Existing money, schedule, rights choices and private reference links are preserved. Suggestions require explicit review and apply before guarded save/publication. Stable requirement IDs connect the brief to delivery mapping and revisions.

features.title: Identity and accounts
features.description: Email signup, password sign-in, GitHub OAuth callbacks, password recovery and authenticated password changes; permanent creator/brand onboarding; preserved internal return destinations; server-validated sessions and role-aware dashboards.

features.title: Creator workspace and portfolio
features.description: Persist creator profile, capability pairs, production workflow and rights offer. Create, edit, preview and publish portfolio items and profile. Upload image, video, audio and text assets, inspect file checks, manage supporting claim evidence and retry expired previews.

features.title: Brand workspace and production briefs
features.description: Persist company details, create/save/reload/edit/publish structured briefs, browse published briefs, inspect candidates in the context of the actual brief, persist shortlists and compare candidates.

features.title: Applications and selection
features.description: Creators apply to the current published brief revision and can withdraw. The brand reviews applications and selects one winner atomically. Engagement creation freezes trusted brief, creator and rights snapshots so later profile edits do not silently change the agreed scope.

features.title: Versioned delivery and acceptance
features.description: Upload ready assets, map files to output requirements and submit immutable delivery versions. Brands request revisions against specific requirements; creators submit a new version. Acceptance requires the latest eligible submission, correct asset ownership/scope and final permissions. Only participants can obtain accepted final download links.

features.title: Responsive and accessible experience
features.description: Responsive landing, discovery, forms and workspace pages; keyboard skip link, visible focus, native menu/film dialogs, Escape dismissal and restored focus; reduced-motion support and pauseable background film; navigation progress, loading indicators, retry controls, upload progress and error recovery.

features.title: Authorization and integrity
features.description: Database row-level security and grants restrict ownership and participant access. Private storage, short-lived signed access, strict request schemas, bounded request bodies, same-origin write guards, optimistic versions, actor-scoped idempotency, quotas and protected database fields enforce workflow rules beyond the UI. Cancelled upload blockers prevent replay until signed-link expiry.

features.title: Private contact management and customer visibility
features.description: Creators and brands can add, edit, reload and clear complete contact records, including names, emails, phones, preferred channel, professional links and postal addresses. The records are separate from public discovery. Database RLS restricts access to the owner, selected collaborators, or explicitly permitted current applicants; withdrawal, rejection and stale revision remove applicant access. Creators view full customer company context on relevant briefs and only authorized contact fields. Brands can view selected creator contact information in engagements.

features.title: AI creator profile optimization
features.description: A real Gateway model analyzes the creator’s profile and actual portfolio descriptions, explains strengths and prioritized gaps, assigns a clearly labeled editorial score, and rewrites the headline and bio without inventing credentials or client results. The creator explicitly consents, reviews each suggestion, applies chosen text to an unsaved draft and saves through existing version checks. Contact fields and private evidence files are excluded from model inputs.

journey: Public evaluator: open /creators, filter the network and inspect a published creator's portfolio, production passport and declared usage offer.

Creator: sign up or sign in, select the creator role during onboarding, complete the profile, add real work and supporting evidence, inspect the checked preview, then publish the portfolio and profile.
Brand: use a separate account with the brand role, save company details, create a six-section brief, resolve readiness issues, save and publish it.
Brand: open creator discovery in the brief context, inspect fit component explanations and rights receipts, save a shortlist and compare up to three candidates.
Creator: open the current brief, apply and describe the proposed pipeline. Brand: review applications and select one creator to create an engagement.
Creator: upload and submit v1 against output requirements. Brand: inspect delivery and request a requirement-specific revision. Creator: submit v2.
Brand: review the latest version and final permissions, accept the delivery and download the accepted files privately. An unrelated account must not be able to access the delivery.

dataModel: accounts links Auth identity to an immutable role. creator_profiles and brand_profiles store role-specific identity. portfolio_items owns assets and claim_signals. briefs owns its requirements, applications and shortlists. Winning application selection creates an engagement with frozen snapshots. submissions stores immutable delivery versions; workflow_events records transitions. catalog_terms supports shared facets and model references; idempotency_keys protects repeat mutations.

verification: Historical baseline evidence: docs/verification.md records 70 unit cases and hosted identity, discovery, rights parity, security, acceptance and signed-upload replay probes; the canonical two-role journey reached accepted exact-byte private downloads.

October 14 implementation review: docs/implementation-review-2026-10-14.md records new email/account/UI checks and explicit gaps in later local full-journey retries. Historical evidence is not a claim that every current user path was retested.

Before this documentation update, the synchronized main source passed TypeScript, ESLint and an optimized production build. This documentation release is checked with build/lint/unit commands and public URL checks as recorded in docs/evaluation-release.md.

Tests and scripts are inspectable in tests/unit, tests/e2e and scripts/test-*.mjs. Browser screenshots and workflow evidence are in docs/evidence. docs/capability-ledger.md and docs/requirements-checklist.md map baseline requirements to evidence.

The contact and AI implementation release adds 16 live Supabase permission/concurrency/request-guard checks and 73 unit cases. Actual production model-call and browser results are recorded in docs/contact-ai-release.md.
limitations: AI generation uses Vercel AI Gateway with server-only credentials or deployment OIDC. Availability depends on the owning Vercel team’s model access and credits. The app returns explicit provider errors rather than substituting a template result. Deterministic checks remain authoritative for publication and acceptance.
Rights receipts compare declarations and references; they do not grant legal clearance. File checks do not verify identity, authorship, licensing or malware safety.

Fictional demo creators and procedural media are explicitly labeled. The initial seed records 12 creators, 24 media items, two brands and three briefs; later tests add scoped fixtures, so these are seed counts rather than live totals.
3D is metadata and poster support; the app does not render 3D models. Media duration/content reviews can require brand review rather than automated byte-level validation.
Payments, escrow, subscriptions, social-platform publishing, follower analytics, blockchain receipts and scope-change orders are outside the implemented workflow.
Email confirmation/recovery delivery depends on the existing Supabase mail setup. The recorded Free-project advisory reports leaked-password protection disabled.

AWS IAM setup is documented as configured and policy-simulated, with no live operator session or active compute. Older run-state and deployment IDs are historical snapshots; use docs/evaluation-release.md for this release.
